title: ICE40ULTRA primitives against a generic SRAM-FPGA capability profile
description: A worked example of the target-catalogue format, written against the ICE40ULTRA gate library that ships in plugins/gate_libraries/definitions. The target is a deliberately GENERIC capability profile (6-input LUTs, dual-port block RAM, DSP blocks, I/O buffers, global clock buffers) and not a specific device: every statement about the target is a profile assumption, and a real migration must replace this file with a device-specific catalogue reviewed against the target vendor's documentation.

review.method: Manual review of every cell in plugins/gate_libraries/definitions/ice40ultra.hgl (cell properties, pin types and ff_config/lut_config) against a generic SRAM-FPGA capability profile. Source-side statements are taken from the gate library itself; target-side statements are profile assumptions.

sources.title: plugins/gate_libraries/definitions/ice40ultra.hgl
sources.note: the HAL gate library this catalogue's source_type names come from; the only source of primitive semantics used here

limitations: No vendor datasheet, device model or toolchain was consulted for either side; nothing in this catalogue is a vendor statement.
The target is a capability profile, not a device: it has no resource counts, no speed grade and no I/O bank rules, so resource fit and timing cannot be assessed against it at all.

The negative-edge flip-flop family (SB_DFFN, SB_DFFNE, SB_DFFNR, SB_DFFNS, SB_DFFNSR, SB_DFFNSS, SB_DFFNER, SB_DFFNES, SB_DFFNESR, SB_DFFNESS) is deliberately NOT covered in this revision: falling-edge capture interacts with the target's clocking rules and was not reviewed. Designs using it are reported as unresolved, which is the intended outcome, not an oversight.
SB_LFOSC, SB_HFOSC, SB_I2C and SB_SPI are hard IP with no generic equivalent and are unresolved by construction.

source.note: source semantics are read from the HAL gate library, never from the primitive names

toolchain.name: generic-fpga-flow
toolchain.note: a placeholder identifying the profile revision; replace with the real toolchain name and version in a device-specific catalogue

target.note: 6-input LUTs with configurable INIT, flip-flops with clock enable and one asynchronous or synchronous reset, dual-port block RAM, DSP/MAC blocks, general purpose I/O buffers and global clock buffers. No hard I2C/SPI, no on-chip oscillator, no PLL is assumed.

capabilities.description: 6-input look-up table with a configurable INIT truth table.
Rising-edge D flip-flop with optional clock enable and one reset or set input, synchronous or asynchronous.
Configurable dual-port block RAM with per-port clock, enable and write enable.
Multiply-accumulate block with optional input, pipeline and output registers.
Dedicated carry logic inside the logic element.
General purpose I/O buffer with optional input and output registers.
Global clock buffer driving a low-skew clock network.
Constant 0/1 sources, usually absorbed by the target synthesis flow.

obligation_templates.title: LUT INIT width and bit order
obligation_templates.description: The ICE40ULTRA gate library declares LUT_INIT with descending bit order for SB_LUT4. A 6-input target LUT holds a wider INIT and may number its bits the other way round, so a copied INIT value is a different function.
obligation_templates.check: Re-derive the target INIT from the source truth table (extend the 16-bit function to the target width and apply the target's bit order), then compare the two truth tables exhaustively - 64 input combinations is a complete check.
obligation_templates.target_assumption: the target LUT is a strict superset of a 4-input LUT and its INIT encoding is documented

mappings.rationale: A 4-input LUT is a subset of a 6-input LUT; the gate library marks SB_LUT4 as c_lut with a LUT_INIT attribute, so the function is fully described by its truth table and carries over.

assumptions.description: The target LUT has at least four inputs and an INIT-configurable truth table.

mappings.rationale: The target has dedicated carry logic, but carry primitives are placement-constrained and their carry-in/carry-out conventions differ. Re-inferring the arithmetic and letting the target flow implement it is normally preferable to a one-to-one mapping.

assumptions.description: The target provides dedicated carry logic reachable from its synthesis flow.

notes: the ICE40ULTRA library types SB_CARRY's pins as 'none', so the carry direction is not readable from the netlist

mappings.rationale: A plain rising-edge D flip-flop; the gate library gives next_state = D and clocked_on = C, both of which the target flip-flop provides.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop captures on the rising clock edge.

mappings.rationale: Clock enable is folded into the next-state function (E & D | !E & IQ) in the gate library, which is exactly the behaviour of a target flip-flop with clock enable.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop has a clock enable that holds the state when deasserted.

mappings.rationale: The gate library models R with clear_on, i.e. as an asynchronous clear. The target flip-flop offers an asynchronous reset, but polarity, recovery/removal timing and whether the target flow prefers a synchronous reset are all open questions.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop provides an asynchronous reset with the same active level.

mappings.rationale: The gate library models S with preset_on, i.e. as an asynchronous preset. Many target families implement set by inverting a reset flip-flop, which changes the power-up state.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop provides an asynchronous set, or a reset flip-flop plus inversion that preserves the observable behaviour.

mappings.rationale: The gate library folds R into the next-state function (D & !R) rather than into clear_on, i.e. it models a synchronous reset. Confirm against the vendor documentation before choosing the target reset flavour.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop provides a synchronous reset, or the reset can be folded into the target's data path without a timing penalty.

mappings.rationale: Synchronous set, folded into the next-state function by the gate library.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop provides a synchronous set or an equivalent data-path transformation.

mappings.rationale: Clock enable plus the asynchronous clear the gate library models with clear_on. The relative priority of enable and reset must be checked in the target primitive.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop's asynchronous reset is independent of its clock enable.

mappings.rationale: Clock enable plus the asynchronous preset the gate library models with preset_on.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop's asynchronous set is independent of its clock enable.

mappings.rationale: Clock enable plus a reset folded into the next-state function; enable/reset priority is a target property.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop's synchronous reset takes priority over its clock enable in the same way as the source.

mappings.rationale: Clock enable plus a set folded into the next-state function.

assumptions.description: The target flip-flop's synchronous set takes priority over its clock enable in the same way as the source.

mappings.rationale: A 4 kbit dual-port block RAM maps onto a target block RAM in principle, but the geometry, the write-mask behaviour and the read-during-write mode all have to come from documentation: the gate library models neither a RAMComponent nor RAMPortComponents for this cell.

assumptions.description: The target provides a dual-port block RAM that can be configured to the required depth and width.

notes: with the ICE40ULTRA library as shipped this mapping is reported as unresolved, because the bit size and port structure it requires are not modelled

mappings.rationale: A 256 kbit single-port RAM with byte-masked writes and power-management inputs. The memory itself has a plausible target equivalent; the STANDBY/SLEEP/POWEROFF controls do not.

assumptions.description: The target provides a single-port memory of at least the same capacity, and the power-management inputs can be tied off without changing behaviour.

mappings.rationale: A fixed-geometry view of the 4 kbit block RAM; the same collision and initialisation questions apply.
A fixed-geometry view of the 4 kbit block RAM; the same collision and initialisation questions apply.
A fixed-geometry view of the 4 kbit block RAM; the same collision and initialisation questions apply.
A fixed-geometry view of the 4 kbit block RAM; the same collision and initialisation questions apply.

A 16x16 MAC block with configurable input/output registers, accumulator and sign extension. A target DSP block can usually be configured to match, but pipeline depth, rounding, saturation and the hold/load controls are configuration, not structure, and none of it is in the netlist.

assumptions.description: The target DSP block can be configured to the same operand width, latency and accumulation behaviour.

mappings.rationale: A general purpose I/O primitive with optional input/output registers and DDR paths. The buffer maps, the constraints do not: I/O standard, drive strength, termination and pin assignment live outside the netlist.

assumptions.description: The target device offers a compatible I/O standard in the bank the pin is assigned to.

mappings.rationale: An I/O primitive that additionally drives a global clock network. Both halves have to hold in the target: a clock-capable pin in the right bank, and enough global clock resources.

assumptions.description: The target package offers a clock-capable pin that can reach the required clock region.

mappings.rationale: A global clock buffer has a target counterpart, but the number of global networks, their reach and the skew they guarantee are device properties. A one-to-one buffer substitution is not a clocking plan.

assumptions.description: The target device has at least as many usable global clock networks as the source design consumes.

mappings.rationale: A constant-0 driver; every target technology has one and synthesis usually absorbs it.
A constant-1 driver; every target technology has one and synthesis usually absorbs it.

An on-chip high-frequency oscillator. The generic target profile assumes no internal oscillator, and frequency accuracy, start-up time and trimming are device properties that no structural match can supply.
unresolved_reasons: the target profile provides no on-chip oscillator, so the design would need an external clock source or a target-specific hard block
the source oscillator's frequency, tolerance and start-up behaviour are not in the netlist

mappings.rationale: An on-chip low-frequency oscillator; same reasoning as SB_HFOSC.
unresolved_reasons: the target profile provides no on-chip oscillator
the source oscillator's frequency and tolerance are not in the netlist

mappings.rationale: A hard I2C controller. Replacing it with a soft core changes the register map, the interrupt behaviour and the protocol timing; there is no structural mapping to propose.
unresolved_reasons: the target profile has no hard I2C block
a soft replacement changes the software-visible register map and must be re-verified against the I2C specification

mappings.rationale: A hard SPI controller; same reasoning as SB_I2C.
unresolved_reasons: the target profile has no hard SPI block
a soft replacement changes the software-visible register map and must be re-verified against the SPI specification

notes: a source primitive that is absent from this table is reported as unresolved: silence is not approval
no entry in this catalogue is a claim that a conversion was performed or that it would meet timing
